controller.name: greedy-root-and-leaf-refinement
controller.rationale: Measured evidence shows every candidate so far lives on a single expanding chain and best_score rises monotonically as that chain is refined: each refinement generation produced strictly better cache policies (0.0006 -> 0.0022 -> 0.0056 -> 0.0091 -> 0.0140 -> 0.0202 -> 0.0260), all from extending the same depth-bonus schedule along one lineage. The winning structural hypothesis is now well established: keeping exact LRU as the primary eviction signal but adding a bounded, depth-scaled recency bonus (evict deeper chain tails first) consistently reduces total recomputed tokens, and increasing the bonus cap along successive tiers has monotonically improved the suite score from 0 to +0.026. The current_version controller wasted budget opening a second root branch early (node 3) that produced only the 0.0 baseline, while the productive branch (node 2 -> 4 -> 6 -> 8 -> 10 -> ...) reached the best results. Revised hypothesis: open exactly one root branch (to satisfy the required distinct-parent shape and explore one independent idea) and otherwise spend every round on parallel refinement of the best-scoring lineage's leaves, ordered by their own score and depth so deeper chain tails -- which the measurements show are cheaper and safer to extend -- get refined first. Ties break deterministically by descending depth then id. This maximizes expected score gain per generation call given the measured monotone trend, while still keeping one new branch per round for diversification. The controller is deterministic, stateless except for tracking the best observed score, and never uses node IDs as predictive features beyond tie-breaking. If the monotone trend reverses on future revisions, the fallback is the recorded best candidate's exact parameterization (8/16/24/32/40/48/56/64 depth-bonus schedule), which is the current measured incumbent at +0.026.

controller.name: dual-branch-depth-bonus-refinement
controller.rationale: Measured evidence is authoritative: the full depth-bonus schedule 8/16/24/32/40/48/56/64 (ids 20/21) is the current best at +0.02603 (128,704 vs LRU 132,144, 3440 tokens saved), and the score has risen monotonically with each extended tier: 8/16 -> +0.0006 (80 saved), 8/16/24 -> +0.0022 (288), 8/16/24/32 -> +0.0056 (736), 8/16/24/32/40 -> +0.0073 (960), 8/16/24/32/40/48 -> +0.0140 (1856), 8/16/24/32/40/48/56 -> +0.0202 (2672), 8/16/24/32/40/48/56/64 -> +0.0260 (3440). The unbounded frequency/recency multiplier (id 1) at -1.34 and the hit-augmented variant (id 9) at +0.00036 are both rejected. Two completed controller revisions (parallel-refinement-code rev 0 and greedy-root-and-leaf-refinement rev 1) both scored +0.0055 in replay and both produced the identical best_score of +0.0260 in 21 attempts over 11 rounds, despite slightly different batch orderings (rev 1 paired 7 with 6, rev 0 paired 6 with 7; both produced functionally identical clones 20/21). This means the controller ordering within the two leaves is not what drives the score -- the candidate generation model is -- and the replay objective value is dominated by N (21 attempts over 11 rounds, beta_calls=0.001, beta_parallel=0.00025). Revised hypothesis: the controller's job is to expose the most informative parents to the generation model in the most productive order. The measurements show the productive lineage runs from node 2 down to 21 via a strict chain (each refinement produced a strictly better policy), while the second root branch (node 3 -> 5 -> 7 -> 9 -> 11 -> ...) produced clones with the same scores but was never the sole driver of improvement. The revised controller therefore: (1) opens root exactly once to establish a fresh branch; (2) prioritizes leaves on the best-scoring path first (descending score, then descending depth, then ascending id for determinism); (3) falls back to non-best leaves by score then depth when workers exceed best-path leaves. This is identical in structure to the prior revision but the hypothesis is now tested against a measured trajectory where the deepest tail on the best path (node 21) and its sibling (node 20) are both at +0.026 and refining either is equally productive -- meaning ordering ties cannot hurt, but keeping both leaves on the best path guarantees the next generation sees the highest-scoring parents. If a future round shows the best path stalling (stagnation > 0 on both leaves), the natural fallback is to open a new root branch (already covered by the workers>leaves case), and if that also stalls, the recorded best parameterization (8/16/24/32/40/48/56/64) remains the incumbent at +0.026. Task flags and node IDs are never used as predictive features; ids appear only as deterministic tie-breaks.

controller.name: exhaustion-aware-chain-refinement
controller.rationale: Measured evidence is authoritative: revisions 3-5 all score 0.0064867527 (20 attempts, 11 rounds, best candidate +0.0260322073, 3440 tokens saved) versus revisions 0-2 at 0.0055094800 (21 attempts) -- the only lever that changed replay value was reducing N (generation calls), since best_score was identical in every replay. Equation 1 charges beta_calls per revealed nonroot attempt and rewards parallel rounds; every trajectory is strictly serial (each round's node depends on the previous round's reveal), so beta_parallel's N/nonempty_rounds term is constant across all controllers and the sole objective lever is N. Counting novel nonroot candidates in the recorded trajectory gives N=18 (ids 1..21 minus the two pure clones id 5 duplicating id 3's policy and id 13 duplicating id 11's policy, and id 4's failed continuation is still a charged attempt), while the reported attempts of 20 include a root-opening slot and one replayed/exhausted slot. Hypothesis: (1) compute N from candidate-signature novelty so clones and replays are recognized as zero-cost and deprioritized to the bottom of the ordering; (2) select only unexhausted legal leaves first (exhausted leaves rank last and are skipped entirely when any alternative exists), ordered by best branch, then ascending stagnation and failure_streak, then least generation-calls, then descending score and depth, ids only as deterministic tie-breaks; (3) leave worker slots EMPTY instead of opening a redundant second root branch -- the measured second branch (3->5->7->9->11->19) produced only clones and never drove improvement, yet inflated N; (4) reopen root only after two consecutive calls without best-score progress, replacing nothing (fill an empty slot) so no productive leaf is sacrificed. This retains every legal-action constraint: distinct integer IDs, root at most once, no internal or max_depth nonroot nodes, and no IDs used as predictive features. The expected replay value is the measured +0.0260322073 best score with N reduced toward 18, i.e. roughly 0.026 + 0.001*2 - 0.00025*18/11 ~ 0.028, versus 0.0065 measured; this is a hypothesis, not a measurement. If clone signatures never appear, behavior degrades gracefully to the validated revision-5 ordering. The recorded incumbent remains +0.0260322073 candidate score.

controller.source:
class ExplorationController:
    """Refine legal leaves on the best-scoring lineage; open root once, early.

    Measured evidence across all completed histories is authoritative. The
    productive signal is the candidate lineage: a strict chain of graduated
    depth-bonus schedules improved monotonically from +0.0006 to the measured
    optimum +0.0475845 (schedule 8/16/24/32/40/48/56/64/72/80/88/96/104/112/120
    with cap 120, 6288 suite tokens saved vs LRU 132,144). Every extension past
    120 regressed (124, 128, 136/144), rollbacks and extreme-tail wraps failed,
    and hit/frequency terms regressed (id 9, +0.00036 vs +0.000605 without).
    The unbounded frequency/recency multiplier (id 1, -1.34) is decisively
    rejected. The controller objective (Section 3 Eq 1) is best revealed score
    minus beta_calls*N plus beta_parallel*N/max(1,nonempty_rounds), so the
    selection policy is: (1) open root exactly once early to establish the
    first branch; (2) thereafter greedily refine legal leaves on the lineage
    containing the best revealed score; (3) tie-break by ascending stagnation
    and failure_streak (avoid replaying exhausted or failed leaves), then
    descending score and depth, then node id for determinism; (4) fill
    remaining worker slots with root only when fewer legal leaves exist than
    workers, never as a stall escape (replay 2 showed stall-triggered root
    reopenings wasted rounds: id 19 lost 1248 tokens). All legal-action
    constraints are enforced: distinct IDs in a batch, root at most once, no
    internal non-root nodes, no non-root nodes at max_depth, root always legal.
    Node IDs are only deterministic tie-breaks, never predictive features.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self.best_id = None
        self.best_score = 0.0
        self.root_opened = False

    def select(self, observed_nodes, round_index, workers, max_depth):
        if not observed_nodes:
            return []
        nodes = {}
        for node in observed_nodes:
            nid = node.get("id")
            if nid is not None:
                nodes[nid] = node
        if 0 not in nodes:
            return []
        # Parent set identifies internal nodes (they already have a child).
        parents = set()
        for node in observed_nodes:
            nid = node.get("id")
            if nid is None or nid == 0:
                continue
            p = node.get("parent")
            if p is not None:
                parents.add(p)
        # Track the best revealed non-root score across calls.
        for node in observed_nodes:
            nid = node.get("id")
            if nid is None or nid == 0:
                continue
            score = node.get("score")
            if score is None:
                continue
            if self.best_id is None or score > self.best_score:
                self.best_score = score
                self.best_id = nid
        # Legal leaves: non-root, no child in observed set, depth < max_depth.
        leaves = []
        for node in observed_nodes:
            nid = node.get("id")
            if nid is None or nid == 0:
                continue
            if nid in parents:
                continue
            if node.get("depth", 0) >= max_depth:
                continue
            leaves.append(nid)

        def path_of(nid):
            path = []
            cur = nid
            seen = set()
            while cur is not None and cur in nodes and cur not in seen:
                seen.add(cur)
                path.append(cur)
                cur = nodes[cur].get("parent")
            return path

        def key(nid):
            node = nodes[nid]
            path = path_of(nid)
            on_best = 0 if (self.best_id is not None and self.best_id in path) else 1
            score = node.get("score")
            if score is None:
                score = -1e18
            st = node.get("stagnation") or 0
            fs = node.get("failure_streak") or 0
            depth = node.get("depth", 0)
            return (on_best, st, fs, -score, -depth, nid)

        leaves.sort(key=key)
        batch = []
        seen_ids = set()
        limit = max(0, int(workers))
        for nid in leaves:
            if len(batch) >= limit:
                break
            if nid not in seen_ids:
                seen_ids.add(nid)
                batch.append(nid)
        root_exhausted = bool(nodes[0].get("exhausted", False))
        # Open root exactly once, early, to establish the first branch.
        # Reopen only to fill a worker slot when no legal leaves remain.
        if not root_exhausted and len(batch) < limit and 0 not in seen_ids:
            if not self.root_opened or len(batch) < limit:
                batch.append(0)
                seen_ids.add(0)
                self.root_opened = True
        return batch
controller.rationale: Measured evidence is authoritative and fully settles the search. Exact LRU and every strict tie-break variant score exactly 0.0. The unbounded frequency/recency multiplier (id 1) scored -1.34, inflating suite extra tokens from 132,144 to 309,856 with catastrophic losses on chat-heavy-00-cap2048 (18,384 to 60,416) and shift-00-cap2048 (8,832 to 52,800); it is decisively rejected. The bounded graduated depth-bonus family is the sole measured-positive region and improved monotonically up to the 8/16/24/32/40/48/56/64/72/80/88/96/104/112/120 schedule with cap 120: 80, 288, 736, 960, 1200, 1856, 2672, 3440, 4112, 4528, 4944, 5424, 5728, 6128, then 6288 suite tokens saved, i.e. +0.0475845 (125,856 vs LRU 132,144), confirmed by many independent identical measurements (best-ever id 12 in the first completed history; ids 12/13/18/20/21 in the second; ids 2/5/6/7/8/9/10/11/12/13/16/17/18/19/20/21 in the third). Every probe past 120 failed and is preserved as falsification: tier 128 regressed to +0.0408040 (three separate runs in the third history and ids 14/15/17 in the second), tier 136/144 scored +0.0340235, tier 124 scored +0.0431045, rollback of depth>=16 to 112 gave +0.0462526, and wrapping depth>=24 to 0 bonus produced -0.0094442 (id 19 second history, 1248 tokens lost). The depth-bonus extension hypothesis past 120 is fully falsified; 120 for depth>=15 is the empirical peak. Adding observed-hit tiers regressed (+0.0003632 vs +0.0006054), so frequency is excluded. The controller objective (Section 3 Eq 1) is best revealed score minus beta_calls*N plus beta_parallel*N/max(1,nonempty_rounds); with beta_calls=0.001 and beta_parallel=0.00025, each additional attempt costs net ~0.001, so the measured controller value of 0.0205 (replays 0.0055/0.0290/0.0271) is what the selection policy yields given 11 rounds and 2 workers per replay. The productive lineage is the chain of improving depth-bonus schedules; the controller opens root once to establish the first branch, then greedily refines legal leaves on the lineage containing the best revealed score, tie-breaking by ascending stagnation and failure_streak (avoiding exhausted and failing leaves), then descending score and depth, then node id for determinism. Root is used only to fill unused worker slots, never as a stall escape: replay 2 showed stall-triggered root reopenings wasted rounds (id 19 lost 1248 tokens) and the second root branch never drove improvement. Revisions 0 and 1 both measured 0.020529 with identical trajectories, confirming that batch ordering among equally-scoring leaves does not change replay value; the productive signal is the candidate lineage, not the specific leaf ordering. This proposal preserves exactly the measured selection policy (open root once early, best-lineage leaf refinement, deterministic tie-breaks), which is the measured incumbent at 0.0205 (controller) and 0.0476 (best revealed candidate). All legal-action constraints are enforced: distinct IDs in a batch, root at most once, no internal non-root nodes, no non-root nodes at max_depth, root always legal regardless of max_depth. Node IDs are only deterministic tie-breaks, never predictive features; task flags are excluded because task category does not guarantee future reuse and no measurement supports task-aware weighting. Hypotheses about future gains are not measurements; the measured incumbent values are 0.0205 (controller, revisions 0 and 1) and 0.0476 (best revealed candidate, schedule 8/16/.../120 cap 120). Plain Python with bounded per-entry work keeps CPU time well within the 2-second wall budget and memory within 256 MiB.
